summary: Johann Friedrich Herbart was a philosopher who studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797). He later held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1802–1841) and taught Eduard Röer.

Johann Gildemeister worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1832–1834) and at Bonn under Georg Freytag, Christian Lassen, and A. W. von Schlegel (~1834–1838). He held professorships at Marburg (~1845–1859) and Bonn (~1859–1890).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at Göttingen (1770–1774), later becoming a professor at the University of Jena (1775) and professor of philosophy at the University of Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald (1808) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1812). He held posts at Greifswald (1815, 1824–1850) and served as professor at Jena (1817–1824).

Johann Gottfried von Herder worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Königsberg (1761) under Immanuel Kant (1762–1764). His career included posts at Riga Cathedral School (1764–1769), Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar (~1776–1803), and Court of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach (1776).

Johann Gustav Stickel worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and archaeology. He studied at Jena (1823–1826) and under Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as professor at Jena (1830–1836).
Johann II Bernoulli studied at the University of Basel (~1724–1729) and later held a post there from approximately 1743 to 1790.

Johann III Bernoulli was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Daniel Bernoulli and attended the universities of Basel (~1757–1758) and Neuchâtel (~1759–1763), later holding memberships at the Prussian, Russian, and Danzig academies.
Johann Jakob Engel was a philosopher who studied at the University of Rostock (~1758–1762) and the University of Leipzig (~1762–1765). He also taught Wilhelm von Humboldt.

Johann Joachim Winckelmann was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the Köllnisches Gymnasium (1736), Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1738–1740), and the University of Jena (1741–1742).
Johann Michael Ackner studied under Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren and Christian Gottlob Heyne from approximately 1805 to 1807.

Johann Tobias Beck worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1822–1826) and held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (~1843–1878).

Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen and the University of Tübingen, later holding mathematics posts at Tartu/Dorpat (~1803–1809), Würzburg (1817), and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1818).

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw worked in Indology and archaeology. She studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. She taught at Groningen (~1947–1951) and Cambridge (1951–1959), and directed Amsterdam's South Asian Archaeology Institute (1958–1983).

Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under Ernst Zinn at Saarland (1951) and under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1971), where she was an assistant from 1973 to 1977.

Johannes Beltz specializes in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed PhD studies by 1999 at the University of Lausanne and École Pratique des Hautes Études under doctoral supervisors Johannes Bronkhorst and Marie-Louise Reiniche.

Johannes Bronkhorst works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at VU Amsterdam, Rajasthan, Pune (under S. D. Joshi), and Leiden. He served as professor at the University of Lausanne from 1987 to 2011 (attested ~1987–2025).

Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1935–1939), held a post at SOAS University of London (~1957–1973), and served as a professor at Leiden University (1978–1986).

Johannes Hertel was an Indologist who completed his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig (1892–1897). He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1919) and held the chair of Indian philology at the University of Leipzig (1919–1937).

Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber and earned a doctorate at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1869–1873). From 1872 to 1889, he advanced from part-time staff to custodian and librarian at the Prussian State Library.
